title: Routing lamina topology profiling
content:
Summary:
This note collects profiling experiments for an internal topology variant we called 'lamina' — a routing + tiling arrangement intended to reduce cross-expert synchronization on long-context requests. Goal was to measure real user-shaped workloads (varied prompt lengths up to 32k tokens) across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen families and to capture where the serving runtime still regresses (p99/p999) vs baseline routing topologies.

Motivation / background:
- Observed high tail latency regressions during long-window bursts for MoE models (esp. when gating churn is high).
- Prior traces implicate: (1) expert handshake delays, (2) uneven kernel launch patterns across GPUs (strided fanout), (3) KV cache eviction pressure in long-context windows.
- Lamina topology: group experts into semi-local shards that prefer intra-group routing for first N tokens, then expand. Idea: reduce cross-device fanout at steady-state while allowing burst redistribution.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Models: llama-33b, mistral-70b, qwen-14b (MoE variants where available).
- Context lengths: 4k, 16k, 32k.
- Routing configs: baseline (global top-k), lamina (group-prefer with expansion=3), conservative (top-1 only), lenient (top-4).
- Hardware: A100-80GB x4 (NVLink), H100-80GB x4 (NVLink), p4d-like config for lightweight checks.
- Batch shapes: single-user interactive (batch 1), synthetic burst (batch 8, random arrival), steady-stream (batch variable up to 16).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency (server-side), per-token CPU/GPU utilization, PCIe/DRAM bandwidth, NVLink counters, kernel occupancy, kernel queue length, KV cache hit rate, routing decision skewness, expert queue lengths.

Important commands / tooling used:
- tcpdump-style trace: runtime-trace --model $M --ctx 32000 --trace-level kernel,timing --out /tmp/lamina/$M-$CFG.trace
- end2end runner: ./bench/e2e_runner --model $M --shape interactive --routing lamina --warmup 100 --samples 1000 --out results/$M-$CFG.json
- flame graphs: pyflame-runtime --input /tmp/lamina/... --gpu-kernels > /tmp/lamina/$M-$CFG.flame.svg
- kernel histograms: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output /tmp/nsys-$ID

Key observations (high level):
1) Tail latency improvements are context- and model-dependent
   - Llama-33b: lamina reduced p99 by ~12% at 16k, ~18% at 32k vs baseline on A100. p999 improvement smaller (~6%).
   - Mistral-70b: lamina showed ~20% p99 improvement at 32k on H100 but increased median by ~4% for batch>4 (extra routing book-keeping).
   - Qwen-14b MoE: mixed — when gating churn > 0.7, lamina reduced p999 by ~25% but increased p95 slightly.

2) Root causes found in traces
   - Expert handshake stalls: when a request requires experts across NVLink partitions, we see serialized CUDA stream stalls waiting on remote memcpy completion (nsys shows wait on device->device).
   - Kernel launch jitter: per-token kernel start times have higher variance with global top-k; lamina groups reduce variance but introduce head-of-line delays during group-expansion phase.
   - KV cache churn: long contexts cause more KV eviction and rehydration for decoder states when routing chooses different expert subsets mid-context. Rehydration cost spikes correspond to p999 events.

3) Resource counters and micro-metrics
   - NVLink utilization increases ~15% for baseline at 32k vs lamina; lamina shifts load to intra-node DRAM and reduces cross-link peaks.
   - Kernel queue length variance is the strongest correlate of tail latency (Spearman rho ~0.68).
   - When gating top-k >1, we see superlinear increase in cross-expert fanout on H100 (likely due to larger warp scheduling interacting with stream ordering).

Deep dive: example trace (Qwen-14b, 32k, burst workload):
- Timeline: token 0..1200 initial warmup (mostly intra-group experts) -> at token ~1245, gating distribution shifts (user input context causes topic change) -> routing expands to 3 more groups -> device A issues 12 remote memcpy ops in quick succession -> device B enters CAS retry loop waiting on handshake tokens -> 180ms tail spike.
- Stack: GPU kernels for FFN/attn overlap poorly because remap kernels block on remote fetch completion; stream serialization occurs in runtime because we conservatively waited for memcpy completion before launching dependent kernels.

Hypotheses & small experiments tried:
- Hypothesis H1: Allow speculative prefetch of likely experts reduces p999 at the cost of extra prefetch bandwidth. Experiment: prefetch top-1 neighbor-experts with TTL 32 tokens. Result: p999 dropped ~14% on average, NVLink up by 8%.
- Hypothesis H2: Switch to asynchronous handshake path to overlap memcpy+kernel launches. Experiment: enable async-handshake flag in runtime. Result: median improved but p999 still dominated by slow memcpy completions on certain NVLink topologies.
- Hypothesis H3: Use KV-affinity routing (prefer experts that retain KV) to reduce rehydration. Experiment: affinity score = alpha * kv_hit + beta * load; alpha tuned 0.7. Result: KV rehydration events reduced by 62% and p999 improved substantially for long contexts on Llama.

Actionable mitigations (short-term):
- Default to lamina-like grouping for long-context routes (>12k) with conservative expansion thresholds. Rollout as runtime flag behind feature gate.
- Add speculative prefetch opt-in for latency-sensitive routes; make it bounded with budget controls (prefetch_budget_per_request).
- Add KV-affinity score to gating heuristics (configurable per-model).
- Instrument kernel queue-length in live tracing and add alerting when variance crosses threshold.

Longer-term / architectural changes to explore:
- Async handshake with prioritized DMA channels: prioritize handshake memcpys for tokens near context boundary. Needs deeper NVLink/driver-level cooperation.
- Hierarchical gating: two-stage gate (coarse group selection -> intra-group fine gate) to avoid cross-shard stranding.
- Model-side hints: asking MoE gater to emit a small hint vector indicating likely expert set for next M tokens (could be trained regression). Works well in simulation but requires model onboarding.

Open questions / mysteries still unresolved:
- Why does Mistral show median regression for batch>4 under lamina? Trace shows extra CPU time doing bookkeeping; need to profile CPU-side routing and lock contention more carefully.
- For some H100 NVLink meshes, async-handshake still blocks due to PCIe fallback paths; need cluster-level mapping experiment.
- We don't yet have reliable synthetic workloads that reproduce real-world gating-churn distributions; need to capture anonymized gating histograms from production.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Run kernel-occupancy sweep with --launch-config eager vs lazy on H100 (blocked by PR #842).
- Add per-request prefetch accounting in telemetry (cost and bandwidth), expose per-customer metric in Console.
- Log gating entropy metric at 1s granularity in trace pipeline (to correlate with p999).
- Longer validation: run 72-hour soak on Dedicated cluster (replicate prod arrival patterns).

Appendix: quick experiment logs (snippets)
